about: How each of the 56 places orders candidates on the printed ballot, by statute. Main source is Ballotpedia's rules page (as of October 2026), which lists one rule per state and often covers only the general election; where it was silent on primaries, the primary is assumed or marked an estimate. NCSL's Order of Names on the Ballot (as of March 3, 2025) is a cross-check only. Territory rules (PR, GU, VI, AS, MP) were not found and are estimates. Statute sections are as Ballotpedia cites them except where a row cites the statute text itself (estimate false); the others are not checked against state code sites.

sources.title: Rules on ballot order and party labeling - Ballotpedia
Order of Names on the Ballot - NCSL (not fetched; cross-check only)
State Board Randomly Determines Ballot Order for 2026 Elections - NC State Board of Elections

US-AK.note: State representative contests use a random draw instead of rotation. Primary is the top-four open primary; rule taken as the same.

US-AL.note: Primary assumed same as general; Ballotpedia gives one rule.

US-AR.note: Draw held by the county board of election commissioners.

US-AS.citation: Source: A.S.C.A. title 6 ch. 6, not confirmed
US-AS.note: Elections are nonpartisan, so no partisan primary; alphabetical assumed. No American Samoa Code section on ballot order has been read, so alphabetical stays an assumption.

US-AZ.note: General: parties by last county gubernatorial vote, then new parties alphabetical, then unaffiliated; names of the same party alternate.

US-CA.note: Secretary of State draws the alphabet; applies to primary and general.

US-CO.note: General: major party, minor party, then other, each group by lot. Primary assumed lot.

US-CT.citation: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 9-249a (general); primary not found
US-CT.note: General settled (9-249a): the party whose candidate for Governor polled the most votes in the last election first, then other gubernatorial parties by votes, minor parties (precedence by office population, then prior sequence, then alphabetical), then petitioning candidates. The primary order for ordinary offices is not settled by the statute text read; lot is kept as an estimate.

US-DE.note: Primary (§ 3124(b)): surnames in alphabetical order under the office title. General (§ 4502(a)(5)-(6)): the Democratic Party column first, the Republican second, any other party in the order the Department decides; unaffiliated candidates alphabetically after the parties.

US-FL.note: General: party of last governor winner first; minor parties in order qualified. Within-party order assumed alphabetical.

US-GA.note: General: party columns by last gubernatorial vote, then alphabetical, independents, write-ins.

US-GU.note: Section 7105(b): each candidate for any office under a party or independent designation is listed according to lots drawn and conducted publicly by the Election Commission after the filing deadline; (c) the nominees appear in columns in the order the lots determine, an incumbent marked with the word Incumbent. Section 7106 applies the same manner to the ballots for all other offices. The chapter sets one rule and does not separate primary from general ballots, so the same lot rule is applied to both.

primary.unit: precinct (alphabetical in the first precinct; the first name moves last in each next precinct)

general.unit: county (the two top parties swap first place by county number parity, alternating by election)

US-IA.note: Primary (§ 43.28): where more candidates seek a nomination than seats, the names are rotated as prescribed by § 49.31; § 49.31(2)(b) arranges them alphabetically in the first precinct and moves the first name last in each succeeding precinct. General (§ 49.31(1)(b)): counties are numbered alphabetically and the top two parties by last vote alternate first place by even or odd county number and election; nonparty organizations placed as the commissioner determines.

primary.unit: ballot form, in the manner the secretary of state determines

general.unit: ballot form, in the manner the secretary of state determines

US-ID.note: Section 34-903(4)(a): the order of candidate names on election ballots for federal, state, county and local offices is rotated in the manner the secretary of state determines for any political entity whose registered voters at the last general election exceeded 25,000 (the state and its large counties); (4)(b): smaller entities apply a random alphabet drawn before each election. Section 34-904 (primary ballots) sets no separate order, so the same rule applies to primaries.

US-IL.note: Filing order; simultaneous filers are ordered by lottery. Ballotpedia lists filing order for both.

US-IN.citation: Ind. Code § 3-11-2-6 (general); primary candidate-name order not found
US-IN.note: General settled (3-11-2-6): the major party whose secretary of state candidate won the most votes in the county goes first on the left, the second major party next, then parties with no candidate for that office and independents in order of petition filing. Primary: 3-10-1-19 orders the offices, not the candidate names; no section found that orders the names within an office, so alphabetical stays an estimate.

US-KY.note: Draw by the secretary of state.

US-MA.note: Incumbents first, then party candidates alphabetical, then others alphabetical.

US-MD.note: Section 9-210(j)(3): in both primary and general elections, when more than one candidate of the same party seeks an office, the names in the group are listed alphabetically by surname (primary Governor/Lieutenant Governor by the gubernatorial candidates surnames). (j)(2): in a general election the majority party first, then the principal minority party, then other parties in descending order of registered voters, then candidates who are not party nominees.

US-MI.note: General: party with the most secretary of state votes first. Within-party order assumed alphabetical.

US-MN.note: President: parties by a vote-average formula, petition candidates random after. Other partisan offices rotate.

US-MO.note: Primary (115.395(2)): names for each office on each party ballot are listed in the order in which they are filed; candidates who file with the secretary of state before 5:00 p.m. on the first day are drawn by random number. General (115.239(1)): the party with the most votes for governor in the left column, the next party to its right, new parties in order of petition filing, independents last by petition date. Names for each office are listed in filing order (115.237(1)).

US-MP.citation: Source: 1 CMC election law, not confirmed
US-MP.note: No source found; assumed alphabetical. The Commonwealth Code election law has not been read. Specimen ballots on votecnmi.gov.mp list candidates in an order that is not alphabetical, so alphabetical is doubtful; the rule is unconfirmed.

US-MS.note: Party candidates first, then others, each alphabetical by surname.

US-NC.citation: N.C. Gen. Stat. 163-165.6; N.C. State Board of Elections 2025 press release
US-NC.note: State Board draws the alphabet direction/letter for all 2026 contests except municipal.

primary.unit: precinct (an algorithm spreads each name across all positions on an equal number of precinct ballots)

US-ND.note: Section 16.1-11-27: the names for each office are first arranged in an order determined by lot by the county auditor, then alternated by an algorithm approved by the secretary of state so that each name is listed in each position on an equal number of precinct ballots across the county, with a separate alternation for state-wide, county-wide and smaller districts; the name order for an office is the same within a precinct. Section 16.1-06-05(4) applies the same alternation to the general election ballot.

primary.unit: precinct (filing order in the first precinct; the first name moves last in each next precinct)

US-NE.note: Primary (32-810): in the first precinct the names are in the order of filing by date and hour; when there are more candidates than vacancies they are rotated precinct by precinct, the first name moving to the bottom each time. General (32-815(1)): the party with the most votes for Governor at the last general election is placed first, the next party second, and so on in descending order, petition candidates beneath all others; where a party has two or more nominees for an office the commissioner or clerk rotates their names by election district.

US-NH.note: Ballotpedia says a random draw picks the first name then alphabetical; NCSL counts it as a random alphabet.

US-NM.note: Primary (1.10.7.9): names of candidates for the same office are ordered by the first letter of the last name in the New Mexico election alphabet, a randomized alphabet the state auditor creates publicly each election cycle (1.10.7.8), ties by later letters and a card draw; candidates designated by convention come first by convention vote (1.10.7.10). General (1.10.6.8): the order of the political parties on the general election ballot is drawn by lot by the state chairs in the secretary of state office in late August; unaffiliated candidates follow; candidates of one party use the election alphabet (1.10.7.9).

US-NY.note: General: parties by last gubernatorial vote; independents by election officials; multi-seat offices may request a draw by lot.

US-OK.note: Primary rotated (absentee order set by the board secretary). General: recognized parties by lot, then unrecognized, then independents, each by lot.

US-PA.citation: Pa. Election Code (25 P.S.) § 2875 (primary); general § 2963 not read
US-PA.note: The Election Code text for the general-election party order (25 P.S. 2963) and the primary lot (25 P.S. 2875) has not been read; secondary reporting says primary positions are drawn by lot. Both rules stay estimates.

US-PR.citation: Source: Ballotpedia and Puerto Rico Electoral Code (Act 58-2020), not confirmed
US-PR.note: Parties thought to be ordered by last gubernatorial vote. Primary order unknown. The Puerto Rico Electoral Code text has not been read; parties by last gubernatorial vote and the primary order remain unconfirmed.

US-RI.note: Primary: party-endorsed candidates first, then unendorsed; if none endorsed, lot. General: party order by lot.

US-SC.note: Partisan general order set by the State Election Commission; primaries alphabetical.

US-SD.note: General: party order and order within a party by draw. Primary assumed lot, not confirmed. The text of SDCL 12-16-3.1 (parties by lot) and 12-16-8 (names by lot) has not been read; secondary reprints agree with the row. The primary rule (chapter 12-6) was not found.

US-TN.note: General columns: majority party, minority party, recognized minor parties, independents.

US-TX.note: Primary order drawn by lot (52.094). General: parties by gubernatorial vote, new parties and unaffiliated by draw.

US-UT.note: Primary assumed the same as general.

US-VA.note: Primary (§ 24.2-529): names appear in the order of time of filing for the office, ties by lot. General (§ 24.2-613(C)): the State Board draws the order of the political parties by lot; candidates of one party appear alphabetically; independents follow in order of filing.

US-VI.note: No source found; assumed alphabetical. The Virgin Islands Code (Title 18) has not been read. The Elections System of the Virgin Islands announces that candidate ballot positions are cast by lot, which points to lot rather than alphabetical, but the statute text has not been read.

US-WA.note: President: parties by last presidential vote. Other offices by draw. Washington has no partisan primary; the top-two primary rule is used.

US-WI.note: Primary (5.62(3)-(4), via 5.60(1)(b)): the elections commission, or the county clerk or board, arranges candidate names by the drawing of lots. General (5.64(1)(b)): party columns left to right by each party candidate vote for president or governor at the last general election, then parties qualifying by petition in order of petition filing, then a column of independents; independent candidates for the same county office are ordered by lot (5.64(1)(e)1).

US-WV.note: General: parties by presidential vote, then by draw.

primary.unit: precinct (each name equally often at top, bottom and each place in a county)

US-WY.note: Section 22-6-122: the names of candidates for each office are rotated on all ballots by precinct for all elections, each name appearing substantially an equal number of times at the top, bottom and each intermediate place in a county (so the primary rotates; the earlier alphabetical assumption was wrong). Section 22-6-121: on the general election ballot party position follows the votes each party got in the county for U.S. representative at the last general election, provisional parties in an order drawn by the secretary of state, independents last in alphabetical order subject to rotation.
